# jj agent

This reference describes the application command parser. See [capabilities](../reference/capabilities.md) for profile and qualification limits.

### Agent capture

Ordinary Git-backed JJ repositories use the local companion metadata store.
Agent capture runs in the CLI process without a native server connection.
`jj agent initialize --request-id <id>` explicitly initializes this metadata;
the first successful enablement can initialize it too. Status and session reads
on an uninitialized repository leave both metadata and actor state absent.

`jj agent sessions [--limit <count>] [--cursor <cursor>]` reads a pinned local
session page. Continue with the returned cursor to keep the same metadata
snapshot across processes. `jj agent receipt <request-id>` returns the original
local capture or initialization receipt. These two commands currently target the
local Git profile. Native repository collaboration reads remain available
through the existing local API.

`jj agent code-evidence --operation <full-operation-id>` inspects one explicitly
selected code operation. Its JSON output includes a typed source reference and
the exact capsule. It stages immutable Git objects without selecting metadata.
Initialize metadata first to establish the source repository identity.

`jj agent associate --request-id <id> --record <association.json>` and
`jj agent checkpoint --request-id <id> --record <checkpoint.json>` accept
complete `CodeAssociationV2` and `AgentCheckpointVersionV2` documents. Use the
source reference from code evidence in each operation anchor; commit anchors
pair that reference with a profile-tagged commit from the capsule. Agent facts
name exact selected sessions and immutable dependencies. Corrections include the
prior version in the record and pass its object ID through `--expected-version`.

Before publication the CLI privately journals the complete request, including
exact capsule bytes. Unknown outcomes retain it.
`jj agent retry-provenance <id>` retries that original request without requiring
the input document or source operation store. A matching durable receipt
completes the journal entry; `jj agent receipt <id>` inspects a completed
request.

`jj agent associations` and `jj agent checkpoints` read bounded local pages with
`--limit` and `--cursor`. Continuations keep one selected metadata snapshot and
cannot move between those catalogs. Reads do not initialize metadata or device
state. Code associations are explicit assertions; hooks currently capture agent
activity without automatically asserting code causality.

`jj agent drain` retries the private sanitized spool in source order using the
repository's backend. Local requests are synchronized before ref publication;
native requests retain their prepared RPC delta. A prepared request cannot move
between those profiles. Unknown outcomes leave the original request pending.

`jj agent status` probes Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode against the exact supported
versions and reports detection, desired enablement, and setup separately.

`jj agent enable --non-interactive --agent <codex|cursor|opencode>` records an
explicit device-local choice. Use `--dry-run` to preview the resulting registry
without changing it. Detection does not authorize every installed harness.

`jj agent setup <codex|cursor|opencode>` installs one enabled, exact-version
integration in the current project. Codex and Cursor receive owned entries in
their existing hook documents; OpenCode receives the namespaced
`.opencode/plugins/jj-store-agent.ts` plugin. Unrelated configuration is
preserved. Use `--dry-run` to preview the target without creating directories,
backups, ownership state, or hooks.

A real setup compiles and caches MongoDB Kingfisher's pinned in-process rules
before installing the hook. The first setup can take longer; later hook
processes reuse the private device-local cache.

The registry is user-restricted, contains no credentials or transcript content,
and is bound to one repository, physical workspace, and stable device identity.
A missing executable, failed probe, or different version is reported without
forwarding harness stderr.

Before changing a project file, setup stores its exact original bytes and the
intended content hash in the device-local registry area. Repeated setup is
idempotent. Status reports a later edit as drifted, and setup refuses to replace
it. Symlinked project configuration paths fail closed.

`jj agent remove <codex|cursor|opencode> [--dry-run]` disables one integration
and removes only its recorded jj-store-owned artifact. It restores the exact
backed-up project file, or deletes a plugin file that did not exist before
setup. Changed target bytes and symlinked paths fail closed. Interrupted cleanup
resumes from the private ownership record; repeated removal is harmless.

Installed hooks call the internal `jj agent hook <codex|cursor|opencode>`
entrypoint. It verifies the enabled registry state, exact owned project artifact
and warmed Kingfisher cache, then sanitizes one bounded standard-input event
before allocating durable source order and enqueuing the sanitized observation.
Invalid or oversized input is represented only by a fixed omission record. Hook
commands produce no normal output and never persist raw input. Pending capture
publication is attempted for three seconds after durable enqueue. An unavailable
native server, unknown outcome, stale request, or timeout leaves the capture in
the private spool without failing the hook; the next hook invocation retries the
oldest exact source-ordered request before later observations.

| `--format <FORMAT>` | Output presentation. JSON retains full identities, versions and response variants for automation. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: text; Values: text, json |
| `--state-dir <STATE_DIR>` | Override device-local state; intended for isolated qualification Inherited by subcommands. |  |
| `-R, --repository <REPOSITORY>` | Path to repository to operate on  By default, Jujutsu searches for the closest .jj/ directory in an ancestor of the current working directory. Inherited by subcommands. |  |
| `--ignore-working-copy <IGNORE_WORKING_COPY>` | Don't snapshot the working copy, and don't update it  By default, Jujutsu snapshots the working copy at the beginning of every command. The working copy is also updated at the end of the command, if the command modified the working-copy commit (`@`). If you want to avoid snapshotting the working copy and instead see a possibly stale working-copy commit, you can use `--ignore-working-copy`. This may be useful e.g. in a command prompt, especially if you have another process that commits the working copy.  Loading the repository at a specific operation with `--at-operation` implies `--ignore-working-copy`. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--no-integrate-operation <NO_INTEGRATE_OPERATION>` | Run the command as usual but don't integrate any operations  When this option is given, the operations will still be created as usual but they will not be integrated to the operation log. The working copy will also not be updated.  The command will print the resulting operation ID. You can pass that to e.g. `jj --at-op` to inspect the resulting repo state, or you can pass it to `jj op restore` to restore the repo to that state. You can also pass the ID to `jj op integrate` to integrate the operation.  Note that this does *not* prevent side effects outside the repo. For example, `jj git push --no-integrate-operation` will still perform the push. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--ignore-immutable <IGNORE_IMMUTABLE>` | Allow rewriting immutable commits  By default, Jujutsu prevents rewriting commits in the configured set of immutable commits. This option disables that check and lets you rewrite any commit but the root commit.  This option only affects the check. It does not affect the `immutable_heads()` revset or the `immutable` template keyword. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--at-operation, --at-op <AT_OPERATION>` | Operation to load the repo at  Operation to load the repo at. By default, Jujutsu loads the repo at the most recent operation, or at the merge of the divergent operations if any.  You can use `--at-op=<operation ID>` to see what the repo looked like at an earlier operation. For example `jj --at-op=<operation ID> st` will show you what `jj st` would have shown you when the given operation had just finished. `--at-op=@` is pretty much the same as the default except that divergent operations will never be merged.  Use `jj op log` to find the operation ID you want. Any unambiguous prefix of the operation ID is enough.  When loading the repo at an earlier operation, the working copy will be ignored, as if `--ignore-working-copy` had been specified.  It is possible to run mutating commands when loading the repo at an earlier operation. Doing that is equivalent to having run concurrent commands starting at the earlier operation. There's rarely a reason to do that, but it is possible. Inherited by subcommands. |  |
| `--debug <DEBUG>` | Enable debug logging Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--color <WHEN>` | When to colorize output Inherited by subcommands. | Values: always, never, debug, auto |
| `--quiet <QUIET>` | Silence non-primary command output  For example, `jj file list` will still list files, but it won't tell you if the working copy was snapshotted or if descendants were rebased.  Warnings and errors will still be printed. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--no-pager <NO_PAGER>` | Disable the pager Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |

For example `jj --at-op=<operation ID> st` will show you what `jj st` would have shown you when the given operation had just finished. `--at-op=@` is pretty much the same as the default except that divergent operations will never be merged.  Use `jj op log` to find the operation ID you want. Any unambiguous prefix of the operation ID is enough.  When loading the repo at an earlier operation, the working copy will be ignored, as if `--ignore-working-copy` had been specified.  It is possible to run mutating commands when loading the repo at an earlier operation. Doing that is equivalent to having run concurrent commands starting at the earlier operation. If you want to avoid snapshotting the working copy and instead see a possibly stale working-copy commit, you can use `--ignore-working-copy`. The working copy will also not be updated.  The command will print the resulting operation ID. For example, `jj git push --no-integrate-operation` will still perform the push. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |

For example `jj --at-op=<operation ID> st` will show you what `jj st` would have shown you when the given operation had just finished. `--at-op=@` is pretty much the same as the default except that divergent operations will never be merged.  Use `jj op log` to find the operation ID you want. Any unambiguous prefix of the operation ID is enough.  When loading the repo at an earlier operation, the working copy will be ignored, as if `--ignore-working-copy` had been specified.  It is possible to run mutating commands when loading the repo at an earlier operation. Doing that is equivalent to having run concurrent commands starting at the earlier operation.
